messages:
kevin: Heads-up: SeleneCorp experienced an isolation window during a peering rollover tonight — ~15min of failed front-end requests. Hosted fallback kept things alive but p95 jumped.

maria: Damn, that sounds like the same symptom cluster we saw in Feb (withdraw + ICMP blackhole).

sasha: Can we get flow logs and peering events? I want to correlate with any BGP withdraws.

kevin: Pasting short LB snippet and customer healthcheck error we captured:
```
2026-03-22T22:14:03Z selene-prod us-east-1 lb1 ERROR conn_reset src=10.12.4.2 dst=172.31.9.44 reason=icmp_frag_needed
2026-03-22T22:14:10Z selene-prod us-east-1 healthcheck FAIL code=504 route=peer-us-east
```

aj: devops-bot: peering events show withdraws at 22:13:58 and 22:14:07 (very brief). auto-fallback to hosted kicked in at 22:14:12. :eyes:

devops-bot: Note: No lost tokens; fallback increased p95 by ~180s for affected requests.

lia: My preliminary hypothesis: MTU or ICMP type blocked on customer edge + our route flap damping. Last time owner rotation caused follow-ups to slip.

maria: Proposed action list (short-lived owners):
- A1: Confirm customer onprem firewall permits ICMP needed for PMTU (owner: sasha) due 2026-03-25 EOD
- A2: Add MTU/ICMP probe to Selene onboarding flow and create an alert on ICMP unreachable spikes (owner: lia) due 2026-03-28
- A3: Change fallback policy to prefer a nearby dedicated fallback pool (preserve SLA) instead of full hosted fallback; make default 2m failover to ded pool (owner: kevin) due 2026-03-26
- A4: Assign recurring-pattern owner and start monthly triage for peering-withdraw patterns (owner: maria) due 2026-04-02

sasha: Will pull flow logs now and reach out to Selene infra lead to request temporary firewall rule access. Marking A1 in progress.

kevin: I'll draft the peering fallback PR today. Plan: add config tag route_policy:dedicated_fallback and a 2m window.

lia: For A2 I'll add metric `peer.icmp_unreach_count` and a 5m anomaly alert. I'll validate in staging with a synthetic.

maria: Two additional housekeeping items:
- A5: Make remediation-owner persistence part of oncall runbook (owner: aj) due 2026-03-30
- A6: Create synthetic that simulates short withdraws and validates fallback behavior (owner: lia+kevin) due 2026-04-05

aj: A5 acknowledged. I'll submit runbook PR and coordinate with product for sprint allocation.

kevin: tagging CS to prep customer-facing message: "we opened remediation items and request a short infra touchpoint" — @maria to own comms?

maria: Yeah I'll draft and send by EOD tomorrow.

devops-bot: Follow-up task list created: https://redwood-internal/tasks/SELENE-POST-1769123999 (items: A1,A2,A3,A4,A5,A6)

kevin: Quick check — could this be our routing policy? I'll validate kernel MTU and peer interface settings in the next maintenance window.

sasha: We'll validate both sides. If Selene blocks ICMP frag-needed then symptoms match. Also check for VXLAN fragmentation on their side.

lia: Adding VXLAN MTU probe to the synthetic test.

maria: Let's reconvene Tue 09:30 to review progress. Owners: update tasks when you start. Ping here for blockers. :white_check_mark:

kevin: PR for A3 opened (draft), will link the task.

sasha: Flow logs uploaded to the incident ticket and shared with Selene contact. Starting A1 now.

aj: Runbook PR queued for review.

lia: Alert + synthetic in staging; will post canary results when ready.

kevin: Thanks — closing check-in for this thread.
